lines.speaker: EMP-01
lines.text: Your count today, Dale. Out with it. Mine's scratched on the axe handle.

lines.speaker: EMP-02
lines.text: Mate, I carry everything you knock down. That's two counts in one. I win on arithmetic.

lines.speaker: EMP-01
lines.text: Carrying isn't felling. Wood doesn't cut itself, and it doesn't count itself either.

lines.speaker: EMP-02
lines.text: Stopped counting at lunch. Lunch was the high point. Everything since has just been wood.

lines.speaker: EMP-02
lines.text: Marta, this one's got a personality. Heavy, stubborn, won't sit right on the shoulder. Reminds me of someone.

lines.speaker: EMP-01
lines.text: If it's like me, it'll reach the cradle before you do.

lines.speaker: EMP-02
lines.text: Twenty years I've known her, and she still can't take a compliment.

lines.speaker: EMP-01
lines.text: Same bet as last week, Dale? Lowest count sharpens both axes before breakfast.

lines.speaker: EMP-02
lines.text: Mate, I've sharpened your axe so often it's practically mine. Fine. Same bet.

lines.speaker: EMP-02
lines.text: Only if lunch counts as a work stoppage. I'm not losing to a sandwich again.

lines.speaker: EMP-01
lines.text: Lunch is twenty minutes. Yours was forty. I timed it.

lines.speaker: EMP-02
lines.text: Twenty days, Marta, and you've not once let me win the count. Not once.

lines.speaker: EMP-01
lines.text: Twenty days and you've not once asked nicely.

lines.speaker: EMP-02
lines.text: Please, Marta. Let me win. There, I asked. Now watch nothing change.

lines.speaker: EMP-01
lines.text: Two more before the light goes, Dale. We've got the time if we don't dawdle.

lines.speaker: EMP-02
lines.text: We could. Or we could eat. Only one of those keeps me alive, Marta.

lines.speaker: EMP-01
lines.text: Ten minutes. Eat walking. I'm counting.

lines.speaker: EMP-02
lines.text: Remember the mill job, the summer it never stopped raining? You swore never again. Look at you now.

lines.speaker: EMP-01
lines.text: Some of us don't learn, Dale. Some of us just buy better boots. Pass the bread.

lines.speaker: EMP-01
lines.text: Priya, read this lean for me. Where does it want to go?

lines.speaker: EMP-03
lines.text: Back and a little left, toward the gap. The crown's heavier on the downhill side.

lines.speaker: EMP-01
lines.text: Good eye. Thicker hinge on the right, then. Watch it go.

lines.speaker: EMP-03
lines.text: Marta, how are your stumps so flat? Mine look like a staircase.

lines.speaker: EMP-01
lines.text: You're rushing the back cut. Level first. Speed comes later, on its own.

lines.speaker: EMP-01
lines.text: Twenty years of ugly stumps first. Yours are better than mine were at your age.

lines.speaker: EMP-03
lines.text: I wrote down your three rules for a back cut. You broke all three today and it still landed perfectly.

lines.speaker: EMP-01
lines.text: Rules are for before you know when to break them. Write that down as well.

lines.speaker: EMP-03
lines.text: Already did. I underlined it twice.

lines.speaker: EMP-01
lines.text: You've been calling the lean before I do lately. When did that start?

lines.speaker: EMP-03
lines.text: About a week ago. I didn't say anything. I wanted to be right a few more times first.

lines.speaker: EMP-01
lines.text: That's the right instinct. Most people brag after the first one.

lines.speaker: EMP-03
lines.text: The lane past the rocks is shorter, but it drains badly. I'd take the long way while it's raining.

lines.speaker: EMP-01
lines.text: Long way costs us minutes on every trip. I'll take wet boots.

lines.speaker: EMP-03
lines.text: Then I'll count how many times you slip. Purely for the notebook.

lines.speaker: EMP-04
lines.text: Marta, sorry, how long until dusk, would you say? Just roughly.

lines.speaker: EMP-01
lines.text: Long enough for three more trunks. Ask me again after the second.

lines.speaker: EMP-04
lines.text: Three. Right. Sorry. I'll stop asking. Probably.

lines.speaker: EMP-01
lines.text: Tomas, your notch is fine. Stop checking it. Cut.

lines.speaker: EMP-04
lines.text: It's fine? Okay. Good. Sorry, it's just that you never say fine.

lines.speaker: EMP-01
lines.text: I said it once. Don't make me sorry I did.

lines.speaker: EMP-04
lines.text: Hold the grab handle past the bend, Marta. The ruts are deep there. I'll keep it in second.

lines.speaker: EMP-01
lines.text: You drive better than you cut, Tomas. That's a compliment. Take it.

lines.speaker: EMP-04
lines.text: Thank you. Really. I'm going to write that one down for Ana.

lines.speaker: EMP-01
lines.text: You stayed out through the last carry today, Tomas. That was good work.

lines.speaker: EMP-04
lines.text: I was nervous the whole time, honestly. But thank you. Is it okay that I was nervous?

lines.speaker: EMP-01
lines.text: Be as nervous as you like. Just keep showing up like that.

lines.speaker: EMP-01
lines.text: We're not heading in yet, Tomas. The light's fine. You keep looking at the sky.

lines.speaker: EMP-04
lines.text: Sorry. I know. I'd just rather be early than late. That's all it is.

lines.speaker: EMP-05
lines.text: Sit down, Marta, love. The trees will still be there in ten minutes. I know, that's the problem.

lines.speaker: EMP-01
lines.text: That's exactly the problem. Ten minutes is a whole trunk.

lines.speaker: EMP-05
lines.text: And ten minutes is a cup of tea. Sit. I'll hold your axe hostage if I have to.

lines.speaker: EMP-01
lines.text: Joan, you're chatting to that tree again.

lines.speaker: EMP-05
lines.text: Somebody has to, love. You only ever talk to them with a blade.

lines.speaker: EMP-05
lines.text: I timed you at supper, Marta. You sat still four whole minutes. A personal best.

lines.speaker: EMP-01
lines.text: Three and a half. I was counting too.

lines.speaker: EMP-05
lines.text: How did you sleep, Marta? And don't tell me you dreamt about hinge wood.

lines.speaker: EMP-01
lines.text: Hinge wood. Clean, even hinge wood. Best night I've had in ages.

lines.speaker: EMP-01
lines.text: Pay's late, Joan. You've gone quiet on me.

lines.speaker: EMP-05
lines.text: When I ran the bar, I counted the till twice before I let myself worry. I'm on my second count.

lines.speaker: EMP-02
lines.text: Priya, settle something. Heavy end first or light end first, through a gap like this?

lines.speaker: EMP-03
lines.text: Heavy end leads. Then the light end swings less behind you. You already knew that.

lines.speaker: EMP-02
lines.text: I did. I just like hearing it said like a textbook.

lines.speaker: EMP-03
lines.text: Dale, Biscuit has sat by your boots at every meal this week. I've been keeping a tally.

lines.speaker: EMP-02
lines.text: That's not data, mate. That's love. Also, I drop things.

lines.speaker: EMP-03
lines.text: Seven dropped crusts at breakfast alone. That is data.

lines.speaker: EMP-02
lines.text: Priya, you're the smartest person on this island. So what's for dinner?

lines.speaker: EMP-03
lines.text: Whatever's on Joan's rota. That isn't intelligence, Dale. It's reading the fridge door.

lines.speaker: EMP-02
lines.text: There's a story going round again. I say it's a deer, or someone's radio. Back me up, Priya.

lines.speaker: EMP-03
lines.text: I can't back you or argue. I wasn't there. Ask whoever was, and ask them which direction.

lines.speaker: EMP-03
lines.text: I'd like to, Dale. But I heard something myself once, and I wrote it down, and it wasn't a radio.

lines.speaker: EMP-03
lines.text: You carried that big trunk from the rocks without setting it down. I paced it out. It's farther than you think.

lines.speaker: EMP-02
lines.text: Don't tell me the number. If you tell me, my back finds out.

lines.speaker: EMP-02
lines.text: Tomas, mate, you take the light end. I'll take the end with the opinions.

lines.speaker: EMP-04
lines.text: Sorry, which end has opinions? Both of them feel heavy to me.

lines.speaker: EMP-02
lines.text: Mine. Mine always has opinions. Lift on three.

lines.speaker: EMP-04
lines.text: Hold on past the bend, Dale. Second gear only through here. Sorry, it's going to bump.

lines.speaker: EMP-02
lines.text: You drive like my nan carried soup, mate. Not a drop spilt.

lines.speaker: EMP-04
lines.text: Is that good? I think that's good. I'm taking it as good.

lines.speaker: EMP-04
lines.text: Dale, can I walk in with you? Not for any reason. Just the company.

lines.speaker: EMP-02
lines.text: Course, mate. I'll talk, you walk, and we're in before the soup's cold.

lines.speaker: EMP-02
lines.text: Writing to Ana again? Tell her her brother's the best driver on the island.

lines.speaker: EMP-04
lines.text: I did, yesterday. Sorry. I also told her you eat for three.

lines.speaker: EMP-02
lines.text: Accurate reporting. Your sister's going places.

lines.speaker: EMP-04
lines.text: Dale, do you think we could head in a bit early today? Just a little bit?

lines.speaker: EMP-02
lines.text: Not yet, mate. Plenty of day up there. I'll tell you when, and I won't forget.

lines.speaker: EMP-02
lines.text: Twenty days in, Tomas, and you still apologise to the trucks.

lines.speaker: EMP-04
lines.text: They've done a lot for us. Somebody ought to say something.

lines.speaker: EMP-05
lines.text: Dale, love, what was that you cooked last night? Biscuit walked away from it.

lines.speaker: EMP-02
lines.text: Biscuit's a critic, not a chef. It was stew. Ambitious stew.

lines.speaker: EMP-05
lines.text: It was brave, sunshine. I'll give it brave.

lines.speaker: EMP-02
lines.text: Cards tonight, Joan? I'm due a win. The universe owes me one.

lines.speaker: EMP-05
lines.text: The universe doesn't owe you, love. I do, and I'm not paying up.

lines.speaker: EMP-05
lines.text: You've been due every night for a week and a half, sunshine. I keep a ledger.

lines.speaker: EMP-05
lines.text: The card tally on the wall's looking very one-sided, Dale. I'd call it settled.

lines.speaker: EMP-02
lines.text: Nothing's settled while there's a deck in the drawer, Joan.

lines.speaker: EMP-02
lines.text: Joan, guess what this log weighs. No, wrong. Heavier than that.

lines.speaker: EMP-05
lines.text: I wasn't going to guess, love. I was going to ask what's for lunch.

lines.speaker: EMP-02
lines.text: Now you're speaking my language. Cheese, if there's any justice.

lines.speaker: EMP-02
lines.text: Paid! Joan, I'm paid! Snacks are on me tonight, and I mean the good ones.

lines.speaker: EMP-05
lines.text: With what you lose at cards, love, you're really buying them for me.

lines.speaker: EMP-04
lines.text: Priya, sorry, that creaking. Is that normal? It sounds close.

lines.speaker: EMP-03
lines.text: Two trunks rubbing, upslope, maybe thirty metres. Listen. It rises with every gust.

lines.speaker: EMP-04
lines.text: Okay. Yes. It does. Thank you. Sorry for jumping.

lines.speaker: EMP-03
lines.text: You took the soft patch in first and didn't spin a wheel. How did you know?

lines.speaker: EMP-04
lines.text: The puddle was flat at the edges, so it's deep mud, not water. Sorry, is that weird to notice?

lines.speaker: EMP-03
lines.text: Not weird. Useful. It's going in the notebook with your name on it.

lines.speaker: EMP-04
lines.text: Priya, when does the light usually go, by your notes? Roughly?

lines.speaker: EMP-03
lines.text: Clear sky, so it holds longer than on the cloudy days. I'll tell you the moment it starts to drop.

lines.speaker: EMP-03
lines.text: Did you finish the letter to Ana? You were on page three last night.

lines.speaker: EMP-04
lines.text: Page five. Sorry, she likes details. I described your notebook. Now she wants one.

lines.speaker: EMP-04
lines.text: Priya, someone said there was something at the treeline. Do you think it's true? Sorry. I keep thinking about it.

lines.speaker: EMP-03
lines.text: I don't know. I didn't see it. Ask whoever said it where they were standing, and when.

lines.speaker: EMP-03
lines.text: I can't tell you what it was. I noticed something once myself and marked the spot. That's all I've got, Tomas.

lines.speaker: EMP-03
lines.text: Breathe out, Tomas. Count the fence posts as we pass. It helps.

lines.speaker: EMP-04
lines.text: One. Two. Okay. It does help a bit. Sorry, I'll count quieter.

lines.speaker: EMP-05
lines.text: Priya, love, rate this one for me. Someone's got a new story about the woods after dark. Evidence or nonsense?

lines.speaker: EMP-03
lines.text: Unverified. One teller, no time, no direction. I'd want a second witness before I wrote it down.

lines.speaker: EMP-05
lines.text: That's why I love you. You turn nonsense into paperwork.

lines.speaker: EMP-03
lines.text: Joan, you said the stew had six ingredients. I counted four and a mystery.

lines.speaker: EMP-05
lines.text: The mystery's love, sunshine. You can't put that in a notebook.

lines.speaker: EMP-03
lines.text: I can. I just wrote 'love, unconfirmed.'

lines.speaker: EMP-05
lines.text: Did you sleep, Priya? I saw that little torch on over your notebook again.

lines.speaker: EMP-03
lines.text: Seven hours. I wrote one line about the wind and went straight back to sleep.

lines.speaker: EMP-03
lines.text: I checked your arcade claims against the board. You're rounding up by two points, Joan.

lines.speaker: EMP-05
lines.text: A bar manager always rounds up, love. It's good for morale.

lines.speaker: EMP-03
lines.text: Then I'll round mine up too, and we can both be wrong together.

lines.speaker: EMP-03
lines.text: The fire pile's leaning north. Keep stacking this side and it'll roll.

lines.speaker: EMP-05
lines.text: Then we stack the other side and blame the wind. Morale and physics, love.

lines.speaker: EMP-05
lines.text: Tomas, sunshine, you're on my team at the arcade tonight. No, you don't get a vote.

lines.speaker: EMP-04
lines.text: Okay. Sorry, I'm not very good. Is that okay?

lines.speaker: EMP-05
lines.text: That's why you're on my team, love. I'm good enough for two.

lines.speaker: EMP-04
lines.text: Joan, did you sleep okay? You always ask me, so I thought I'd ask first.

lines.speaker: EMP-05
lines.text: Like a log, love. Fitting, for the job. And you?

lines.speaker: EMP-04
lines.text: Mostly. Sorry. Better than the first week, anyway.

lines.speaker: EMP-05
lines.text: Eat something before we go in, Tomas. You've got a face like a wet Tuesday.

lines.speaker: EMP-04
lines.text: Sorry. I just don't like it when the light starts going. I'll eat. I promise.

lines.speaker: EMP-04
lines.text: Joan, I beat your score on the second machine. Sorry. I didn't mean to.

lines.speaker: EMP-05
lines.text: Never apologise for a high score, sunshine. Apologise for that haircut.

lines.speaker: EMP-04
lines.text: You gave me the haircut.

lines.speaker: EMP-05
lines.text: Go on, Tomas, tell me about the gears again. I find it soothing.

lines.speaker: EMP-04
lines.text: Really? Okay. Third is fine on the flat, but this truck hates second on a hill. You can feel it sulk.

lines.speaker: any
lines.text: Your end's dipping. Lift a bit or we'll both be wearing it.

lines.speaker: any
lines.text: My end's fine. It's your end telling stories.

lines.speaker: trait:sociable
lines.text: So where are you from, then? Properly, not what's on the company form.

lines.speaker: any
lines.text: Small place. You'd drive through and never notice. That's the charm of it.

lines.speaker: trait:timid
lines.text: Is it me, or is the light going early tonight?

lines.speaker: trait:level_headed
lines.text: Same as yesterday. Keep walking and we'll be in with the others soon enough.

lines.speaker: trait:stronger
lines.text: Swap ends? I've got more left in me than this log has.

lines.speaker: any
lines.text: Not a chance. I'm not handing you the bragging rights.

lines.speaker: trait:observant
lines.text: Somebody's left a glove on that stump back there. Not mine.

lines.speaker: any
lines.text: Not mine either. Hang it on the fence post. Someone'll claim it.

lines.speaker: trait:reliable_driver
lines.text: Brace your feet. Ruts ahead. I'll keep her slow.

lines.speaker: any
lines.text: Slow is good. Slow is my favourite speed.

lines.speaker: trait:skeptical
lines.text: Heard the latest story? Third time it's changed. By next week it'll be wearing a hat.

lines.speaker: any
lines.text: Stories grow out here. There's not much else to do after dark.

lines.speaker: trait:hard_working
lines.text: Next one's ready. You notch, I'll clear the brush.

lines.speaker: any
lines.text: Deal. Shout before it goes.
